meta.title: Requirements — Bathtub Wastewater Overflow Trip Lever
meta.provenance_note: Each requirement restates a statement in the project brief (2026-11-06 session). No requirements were inferred beyond the brief. See project/README.md.

requirements.requirement: Bathtub wastewater overflow trip lever is stuck inside the hidden plumbing behind the wall and must be removed/repaired.
The overflow is in a hard-to-access area; opening drywall to reach the plumbing is a possible but non-preferred outcome.
5+ licensed plumbers have already been unable to remove it from above without concern over destroying the hidden plumbing behind the wall.
Removal from above is the preferred outcome if a provider can perform it safely.
If above-access is not possible, the accepted approach recommended by consulted plumbers is working from below.
The space below is a storage unit; below-floor work may require opening the drywall ceiling to access the hidden plumbing.
A single coordinated service must perform both the plumbing work and the drywall (ceiling) opening and restoration — one accountable vendor for both trades.
The vendor must be a licensed plumber or contractor.
The vendor must service San Francisco.
Vendor must have experience doing delicate work in a sensitive environment: the unit is tenant-occupied.
Candidate vendors must be surfaced from review-backed services (e.g., Yelp and similar review platforms) for this specific type of work.
Reference photos of the work area may be supplied later; until then, planning proceeds from the written description only.
Collect, organize, and analyze the full requirements list plus the three received estimates into a reviewable dashboard with per-row source links.
Every published data row must carry a source link; values that cannot be confirmed from an official source are left blank and flagged as unverified — never inferred.
